subject: Polylink renewal: regional reserved pools and throughput commitments
messages:
From: Emma Barnes <emma@polylink.io>
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@polylink.io
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Renewal discussion — adding EU & APAC reserved pools

Hi Vanessa,

As we near our renewal window (Aug 15), the product and infra teams here at Polylink want to expand our Dedicated commitment to add both an EU pool and an APAC pool. Current usage has spiked in EMEA and APAC and we are seeing a 2.6x increase in p95 tail latency when traffic hits cross-region endpoints.

High-level asks:
- Add +8 GPUs in EU (preference: H100 or equivalent) and +6 GPUs in APAC (A100 acceptable) as reserved pools.
- Throughput guarantee: support sustained 300 tok/s across the EU pool with burst headroom to 450 tok/s; APAC target p95 latency < 250ms for short-chat workloads.
- Clear failover behavior: if EU pool is saturated, route traffic to US with a note on expected additional latency and model variant fallback.

We want to lock term changes into the renewal so we can start capacity planning and procurement on our end. Can Redwood provide a proposed AM (action plan), an ETA for capacity availability, and any SLA tweaks? Procurement also needs a redline copy of the amendment to review.

Thanks — happy to sync over a short call this week.

—Emma
Emma Barnes
Head of Ad Ops, Polylink
Emma@polylink.io

Attachments: none (will request MMP from procurement)
From: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai

Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 12:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — adding EU & APAC reserved pools

Hi Emma — thanks for the clear ask and timeline.

Short answers up front:
- We can add regional reserved pools for EU and APAC at renewal.
- We support both H100 and A100 families; H100 gives better headroom for long-context workloads.
- We can commit to a throughput/latency target in the contract for the EU pool (p95 latency target and a throughput SLA), with an associated pricing uplift.

Next steps I propose:
1) Internal scoping and cost estimate (we’ll map exact GPU mix and instance sizing) — Karthik, can you run a capacity mapping and indicate whether the EU +8 H100 / APAC +6 A100 ask maps to our reserved SKU stack and what the expected uplift is?
2) Failover behavior: Vivek, can you draft a recommended failover policy (regional routing, cache warm-warm approach, and estimated added latency when routing to US) we can include in the amendment?
3) I’ll produce a Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and a term-amendment delta for procurement to redline.

Emma — can you confirm whether Polylink needs hard p95 latency guarantees or a throughput SLA (or both)? Also confirm whether the APAC pool can accept A100 instead of H100.

If that works I’ll schedule a 30-minute sync for Thurs. Attaching a blank MAP template in the follow-up once internal scoping is done.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Director, Redwood Inference

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai

Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 08:30:00 +0000
Subject: RE: Renewal discussion — adding EU & APAC reserved pools (scoping notes)

Vanessa / team — quick scoping notes based on Polylink numbers and our capacity templates: 

1) GPU mapping and sizing:
- EU: +8 H100-equivalent nodes -> maps to two reserved pools of 4xH100 each (preferred). This gives better sustained throughput for long-context rerank/generation.
- APAC: +6 A100 nodes -> can be a single pool (6xA100) with autoscale burst to spot capacity if allowed.

2) Throughput / latency planning:
- For the short-chat workload described (average 120 tokens per request), target sustained throughput for EU pool at 300 tok/s is feasible with the H100 mapping. Expect p95 latency ~160–220ms under normal conditions; under sustained bursts p95 may move towards 260–320ms depending on batching and KV cache hit rate.
- APAC with A100 should comfortably meet p95 <250ms for short-chat at the requested traffic volumes if we enable prefix caching and a 2–3 request batching window.

3) SLA framing / SLOs:
- We should offer: throughput SLA (e.g., 99% of minutes >= 70% of committed tok/s) + latency SLO (p95 target with credits tied to sustained breach windows). Exact thresholds and credit formula to be handed to Sales/Legal for the amendment.

4) Timeline & runway:
- Lead time for reserved pools (with node procurement and scheduling) is ~6–8 weeks post-signature for guaranteed H100 racks in EU; APAC A100 pool could be available in ~4–6 weeks.

I’ll prepare a capacity worksheet and cost uplift estimate (attach capacity_mapping_H100_A100.xlsx) for inclusion in the MAP.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 25 Jul 2026 15:10:00 +0000
Subject: RE: Renewal discussion — adding EU & APAC reserved pools (failover + routing)

Couple of operational notes to include in the MAP and amendment:

1) Failover policy (recommended):
- Primary routing: region-local pool (EU or APAC).
- Overflow: if 95th percentile of request queue length or CPU/GPU utilization crosses threshold for >2 minutes, begin spillover to US pool.
- Fallback model variant: on spillover we recommend an equivalent-quantized model variant (smaller footprint) that preserves 95% of intent quality but reduces token-time by ~30% — documented in the MAP.

2) Cache & warm-warm strategy:
- Warm caches by periodically pre-warming common prefixes during nightly low-traffic windows in the target region. Maintain two-minute rolling KV cache replication to reduce cold-miss impact on failover.

3) Observable guarantees / runbook:
- Add a runbook entry that explains routing decisions and the consumer-visible message: "Traffic is being routed to a backup region; expected additional latency +120–200ms and possible minor differences in output due to a quantized fallback model."
- Include an incident SLA for cross-region failover testing windows (quarterly scheduled DR drills).

4) Risk & mitigation:
- Risk: cross-region egress + transient cache misses. Mitigation: short-term burst capacity in reserved pools and a pre-authorized burst clause in the amendment for up to 20% extra capacity for 72-hour windows.

I recommend we include these operational guarantees as part of the commercial term (runbook as an exhibit) rather than burying them in an internal ops doc.

Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Product Ops, Redwood Inference

Emma / Polylink procurement team — thanks for the discussion earlier. Attached is an updated Mutual Action Plan (Polylink_MUTUAL_ACTION_PLAN_v2.pdf) and the capacity worksheet (capacity_mapping_H100_A100.xlsx). Summary of commitments for inclusion in the amendment: 

1) Capacity & timing:
- EU reserved pool: +8 H100-equivalent nodes, target availability 6–8 weeks post-signature.
- APAC reserved pool: +6 A100 nodes, target availability 4–6 weeks post-signature.

2) SLA / SLOs:
- Throughput SLA: 99% of minutes >= 70% of committed tok/s (EU pool target 300 tok/s sustained).
- Latency SLO: EU p95 target ~220ms (contingent on prefix cache hit rates); APAC p95 <250ms. Credit mechanics are in Section 3 of the MAP.

3) Failover & runbook:
- Overflow spill to US pool after 2-minute sustained saturation; expected added latency +120–200ms and fallback to a quantized model variant documented in Exhibit B (runbook).
- Quarterly failover DR drills; Redwood provides runbook and test plan.

4) Commercials & term:
- Proposed term uplift: 12-month renewal with committed reserved nodes as above. Pricing uplift and an optional 20% temporary burst clause for 72-hour windows are included in the attached MAP.

Next steps:
- Procurement: please review and redline the amendment in the attached MAP. We can add the Runbook as Exhibit B in the contract.
- I’ve shared a DocuSign link for the amendment draft: https://docusign.com/Polylink/POLY-4721-signature
- If procurement needs formal pricing sheet, I can attach the line-item cost breakdown (available on request).

Would love to lock timelines so our capacity planning can prioritize EU H100 racks. Suggest we aim to sign by Aug 20 to meet the lead time.

Thanks,
